A large scheme may be subdivided to keep title plans manageable.
Each separately registered part of a subdivided scheme receives its own reference.
Each addition normally includes an extract from the scheme plan.
A separate extract is unnecessary when the scheme-plan extract is already the deed plan inducing registration.
HM Land Registry may prepare a memorandum of understanding for application handling.
The first parcel application causes a title number to be allocated.
Later additions are amalgamated with the allocated scheme title.
Separate titles may be created where different classes of title must be granted.
Subordinate leasehold or rentcharge titles should be closed after acquiring the superior interest.
Possessory titles should be upgraded when appropriate evidence is available.
Land in a stopped-up road or way may be added where both sides are acquired for redevelopment.
The original or an official copy of a stopping-up order and its plan should support the application.
First-registration applications must give full particulars of incumbrances.
Restrictive covenants subsisting at acquisition must be disclosed.
Easements subsisting at acquisition must be disclosed.
Planning authority to develop does not normally extinguish private third-party rights.
The applicant should notify HM Land Registry when all scheme land has been acquired.
HM Land Registry will not normally maintain a scheme with no addition application for six months.
Scheduled-monument data covers historic buildings and sites.
Examples include Roman remains, burial mounds, castles, bridges, earthworks, deserted villages and industrial sites.
Scheduled monuments can be designated by the Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.
Historic England keeps and maintains the scheduled-monument list.
The live scheduled-monument dataset reports 20,150 records.
The scheduled-monument dataset reports one provider.
Its collector last ran on 27 July 2026.
New scheduled-monument data was last found on 25 July 2026.
The dataset contains some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
The scheduled-monument dataset is licensed under OGL version 3.0.
A building preservation notice takes effect immediately.
A local planning authority may serve a notice where demolition threatens special character.
A local planning authority may serve a notice where alteration threatens special character.
A notice temporarily protects the building as if it were listed.
The authority must apply to Historic England for listing when serving the notice.
The live building-preservation-notice dataset reports nine notices.
Its collector last ran on 28 July 2026.
New building-preservation-notice data was last found on 17 July 2026.
A locally listed building or site can make a positive contribution to local character.
Local listing can recognise contribution to a sense of place.
Local listing is based on heritage value.
A locally listed asset need not be nationally designated.
A locally listed asset need not be inside a conservation area.
A local planning authority may give an asset protection through a formally adopted local list.
The current locally-listed-building dataset is experimental.
The live dataset reports 448 locally listed buildings.

The national-park dataset represents administrative boundaries of national park authorities.
The dataset covers national park authority boundaries in England.
The boundaries are provided by the Office for National Statistics.
The stated purpose is production of statistics.
